author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both the HTML page and the reinstated machine-readable endpoint
summary: Narrow the published veterinarian directory to only the veterinarians holding a named specialty, on both the paged HTML page and the machine-readable form (reinstated as a supported surface). Match a whole specialty name, case-insensitive; an absent, empty, or whitespace-only name returns the full directory unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the HTML page is narrowed to it, only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time.
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable form is narrowed to it, only those veterinarians are returned.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; a value that is only the beginning of a specialty does not match.
Given a name no veterinarian's specialty equals, either form returns a normal, successful response (HTTP 200) listing no veterinarians.
Given an absent, empty, or whitespace-only specialty, either form returns the full directory as though no narrowing were asked, matching how owner search treats an empty term.
Given a narrowed HTML result spanning more than one page, following a pagination link preserves the narrowing and the next page shows only matching veterinarians.
Without the specialty parameter, both forms behave exactly as before.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search remains out of scope (NG-9, narrowed 2026-08-26).
No on-page filter control (form, dropdown, or other UI) this round; the narrowing is requested through the address alone.
Narrowing by more than one specialty in a single request is unspecified (open question).
notes: URL contract only. HTML surface: /vets.html?specialty=<name>. Machine-readable surface: /vets?specialty=<name>, reinstated as supported (the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id is not reused). Empty or whitespace-only value is treated as absent. No-match yields HTTP 200 with an empty veterinarian list. Two open questions recorded in the PRD: whether the machine-readable form paginates a narrowed result (narrowest reading: returns the whole matching set), and how a repeated specialty parameter is treated (narrowest reading: honor one). ADR: docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. Note: docs/adr/README.md index row for this ADR is outside product-requirements-expert write scope and still needs adding by the owner.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Adds an optional specialty filter to both veterinarian directory surfaces by mirroring the existing owner-search filtering pattern (system-design Contracts: OwnerController/OwnerRepository) inside the vet feature package. No new module, no new pattern, no service layer introduced. It is a parameter plus a filtered repository query on the existing feature-package + Spring Data derived-query shape. The 'why' (NG-9 narrowing and machine-readable route reinstatement) is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md, so no new ADR is warranted. system-design.md updated: VetController/VetRepository Implements now include REQ-VET-003, and the Known Defects row that called the machine-readable route unrequested-and-pending-removal is marked resolved by the 2026-08-26 ADR. Basis: grep/Read of VetController.java, VetRepository.java, OwnerController.java, OwnerRepository.java (IDE oracle not connected).
integration_points: VetRepository gains two filtered finders: a paged Page<Vet> for /vets.html and an unpaged Collection<Vet> for /vets. Suggested derived-query names: findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String). Distinct is required because the vet_specialties ManyToMany join can duplicate a Vet row; NameIgnoreCase gives the whole-name, case-insensitive, non-prefix match the PRD requires.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each take @RequestParam(required=false) String specialty. Branch exactly like OwnerController.processFindForm: null/blank after strip() -> existing findAll paths unchanged; non-blank -> filtered finder. HTML path stays paginated over the filtered Page; JSON path returns the whole matching Collection (narrowest reading of the open pagination question in the prd-entry).
VetController.addPaginationModel must place the active specialty on the Model so vetList.html can carry it; findPaginated(page) becomes findPaginated(page, specialty).

vetList.html pagination hrefs (currently '/vets.html?page=__${i}__' etc.) must append the specialty query parameter when present, so following a page link preserves the narrowing — the same obligation owner pagination already meets.

patterns.description: Blank-as-absent filtering: read the param, null -> "" (broadest), else strip(); page via PageRequest.of(page-1, pageSize). Mirror this control flow for specialty. Note the blank sentinel differs: owner passes "" to a StartingWith query (empty prefix matches all); for vets a blank specialty must route to the UNFILTERED findAll path, since an empty-string equality match would return nothing.
Spring Data derived query returning Page<Owner>; the vet filtered finders follow the same declarative derived-query shape (no @Query needed).

risks.risk: Distinct + Pageable over the EAGER ManyToMany specialties collection can trigger Hibernate to apply pagination in memory (HHH000104), because a fetch-join with a collection cannot be paged in SQL.
risks.mitigation: Acceptable at the seeded scale (six vets). If it must be eliminated, express the filter with an EXISTS/member subquery JPQL that filters on specialty name without fetch-joining the collection, so the page is applied in SQL. Not blocking for this slice.

risks.risk: VetRepository.findAll is @Cacheable("vets") with no eviction (Open Question #5). New filtered finders that are also cached add unevicted cache entries keyed by specialty (and pageable).
risks.mitigation: Mirror @Cacheable("vets") for consistency — the default key includes the specialty/pageable args, so entries are distinct and correct. This is consistent with the existing read-only, no-write-path vet data; it does not widen the open question. Leaving the filtered finders uncached is equally acceptable.

notes: No new ADR: the decision rationale is fully captured in docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md, and the filtering itself reuses the owner-search pattern (not hard-to-reverse or surprising). The prd-entry's two open questions take the narrowest reading (JSON returns the whole matching set unpaged; a repeated specialty param honors one) until a consumer forces otherwise. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records present.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Defense-in-depth (not currently exploitable): the pagination hrefs interpolate the user-derived specialty into the @{...} link via Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${specialtyQuery}__). Preprocessing re-parses the substituted text as a Thymeleaf/SpEL expression, which is the canonical Thymeleaf SSTI antipattern, and the concatenated value is neither URL-encoded nor passed as a link parameter. It is not concretely exploitable here: the specialty only reaches this sink when totalPages>1, which requires it to exactly (case-insensitively) equal a stored specialty name (the repository finder is an equality match, not Containing/StartingWith), so the reflected value is constrained to the trusted set of seeded specialty names and cannot carry an injection payload; Thymeleaf also HTML-escapes the attribute on output. The pattern becomes exploitable if the match is ever loosened to a prefix/substring or if specialty names become user-writable.
findings.fix: Pass specialty as a proper link-expression parameter so Thymeleaf URL-encodes it and never re-parses it as an expression, e.g. th:href="@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}" (omit the param when specialty is null), replacing the string-preprocessing __${specialtyQuery}__ form.

approved_aspects: Repository filtering uses a Spring Data derived finder (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) with bound parameters - no @Query string concatenation, so no SQL injection
specialty is normalized (null/empty/whitespace collapse to null 'no narrowing'); page remains a bounded int with defaultValue
JSON /vets handler reflects specialty only into the parameterized query, never into a template - no reflection sink
Finders are @Transactional(readOnly=true); the change adds no write path and no data-integrity risk
No dependency or build changes - no new supply-chain / CVE surface introduced

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Specialty parameter is embedded in pagination hrefs via raw string concatenation (`'&specialty=' + specialty`) without URL encoding. All five pagination links use the `__${specialtyQuery}__` preprocessing approach, which inlines the value as a literal string before Thymeleaf processes the `@{...}` URL expression. Thymeleaf only URL-encodes values expressed with the `(param=value)` parameter syntax; a preprocessed string bypasses that step. For the current seeded specialty names (ASCII words), the URLs happen to be correct. For any specialty name that contains a space, `+`, `&`, `%`, or non-ASCII characters, the generated href is malformed and the filter breaks silently. The idiomatic Thymeleaf 3 fix applies to all five `th:href` attributes and to the `th:with` expression that constructs the shared query fragment.
findings.fix: Replace the `th:with` specialtyQuery variable and all five `th:href` preprocessing expressions with the `(param=value)` parameter syntax, for example `th:href="@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}"`. Thymeleaf omits parameters whose value is null, so the `th:with` guard and the `specialtyQuery` variable can be removed entirely. Apply the same substitution to the first-page, previous-page, next-page, and last-page links.

approved_aspects: VetRepository derived-query names are precise and self-documenting; Javadoc covers the Distinct rationale and the case-insensitive matching contract
VetController.normalizeSpecialty has a single responsibility, is correctly placed as a private helper, and its Javadoc states the blank-as-absent contract unambiguously
The findPaginated comment explaining why blank routes to the unfiltered path (unlike the owner prefix pattern) preserves a non-obvious decision for the next reader
Constructor injection used throughout; no @Autowired annotation
@Transactional(readOnly=true) and @Cacheable(vets) applied consistently to the two new finders, mirroring the existing findAll methods
showVetList correctly guards the model attribute so specialty is only present when active, which is exactly what the template null-check expects
showResourcesVetList branches cleanly on normalizeSpecialty output with no duplication
Test method names in VetControllerTests read as behaviour specifications (the...should... form)
ClinicServiceTests covers whole-name match, prefix non-match, no-match empty return, paged variant, and case-insensitivity — all key boundary conditions for the repository layer

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: No HTTP-layer test covers the no-match case for either surface. PRD acceptance criterion 'given a name that no veterinarian's specialty equals, when either form is narrowed to it, then the response is a normal, successful page or document listing no veterinarians' is verified only at the repository layer (ClinicServiceTests). The controller's rendering of an empty paged result (HTML) and an empty vetList (JSON) is never exercised at the @WebMvcTest level. Because the mocked VetRepository returns null by default for any unstubbed Page<Vet> method, a test for a non-matching specialty (e.g. 'cardiology') at the web layer would also serve as a regression guard against a NullPointerException in the controller's pagination code should the null-safety assumption ever break.

Blank/whitespace specialty is tested for the HTML surface (theBlankSpecialtyShouldReturnTheFullDirectory uses param '   ') but the JSON surface has no equivalent test. PRD criterion 'given an absent, empty, or whitespace-only specialty name, when either form is requested, then the full directory is returned as though no narrowing were asked' requires coverage of the /vets JSON endpoint with a blank specialty parameter.

thePaginationLinksShouldCarryTheSpecialtyAcrossPages uses containsString("specialty=surgery") which passes if the string appears anywhere in the rendered page — in the model, in a hidden input, or in any rendered attribute — not specifically in pagination link hrefs. A tighter assertion such as containsString("page=2") combined with containsString("specialty=surgery"), or a regex matching a pagination anchor href, would more precisely verify that the pagination links themselves carry the parameter across pages rather than just that the value is present somewhere in the page output.
findings.fix: Change the assertion to verify the specialty value appears specifically in a pagination href, e.g. use containsString("?page=2&specialty=surgery") or an equivalent path-and-param form matching the template's generated URLs.

approved_aspects: Test distribution is sound: repository-semantic tests (case-insensitive whole-name match, prefix non-match, no-match empty result, paged variant) are placed in ClinicServiceTests under @DataJpaTest using a real H2 database, which is the only layer where the actual derived-query semantics can be genuinely exercised. @WebMvcTest cannot exercise match semantics through a mocked repository, so moving those tests to the service layer is correct.
BDD naming convention (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) is followed for all eight new REQ-VET-003 tests across both files.
Real-DB tests in ClinicServiceTests use meaningful Tier-1 test data values ('RaDiOlOgY', 'radio', 'cardiology', 'SURGERY') that directly express the tested specialty, with no mystery literals.

AssertJ collection assertions (containsExactlyInAnyOrder, isEmpty) are used correctly in ClinicServiceTests. MockMvc result matchers and Hamcrest string matchers are idiomatic for the @WebMvcTest layer.

theVetListShouldShowOnlyVeterinariansHoldingTheGivenSpecialty verifies both inclusion (Helen Leary) and exclusion (James Carter) in the HTML content and also asserts that the 'specialty' model attribute is present, which is a prerequisite for the Thymeleaf template to render pagination links correctly.
Factory methods james() and helen() in VetControllerTests encapsulate Vet construction and make test intent clear at the call site.
